title: Narrative Techniques
description: How authors craft stories using perspective, structure, and voice.

notes.heading: Point of View
notes.body: First person uses "I/me" — feels personal. Third person limited follows one character. Third person omniscient knows all characters' thoughts. POV shapes what the reader knows and how much they trust the narrator.

notes.heading: Narrative Structure
notes.body: Most stories follow: exposition (setup) → rising action (conflict builds) → climax (peak tension) → falling action → resolution. This is Freytag's Pyramid. Some authors play with this order for suspense.

notes.heading: Foreshadowing and Flashback
notes.body: Foreshadowing: hints early about later events. Flashback: jumps back in time to show earlier events. Both control what readers know and when.

flashcards.definition: Uses "I/me" — reader only knows what this character knows.
All-knowing narrator who can describe any character's thoughts and feelings.
Moment of highest tension — the turning point.
flashcards.example: In a detective story, when the murderer is revealed.

flashcards.definition: Hints given early about events that will happen later.
flashcards.example: A dark storm arriving as the hero sets off on a dangerous journey.

flashcards.definition: A scene interrupting present action to show an earlier event.

questions.stem: Which POV uses "I" and limits the reader to one character's perspective?
questions.explanation: First person uses "I" and places the reader inside one character's mind.

questions.stem: The turning point of highest tension in a narrative is the:
questions.explanation: Climax is the peak of the story's tension.

questions.stem: A childhood memory scene in the middle of a present-day story is a:
questions.explanation: A flashback interrupts current timeline to show a past scene.

questions.stem: A cracked bridge railing early in a story hinting at later collapse is:
questions.explanation: Foreshadowing plants hints about future events.

questions.stem: Which stage introduces characters, setting, and initial situation?
questions.explanation: Exposition sets the scene and introduces key characters.
